newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela lawmakers set to consider labor reforms. [CORRECTED 22:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Venezuela lawmakers set to consider labor reforms. [CORRECTED 22:55 GMT]

text.p: The Venezuelan Congress is set to begin consideration of a labor reform agreement reached late last month by the government, private businesses and union officials, Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff said on Monday.
"The government will present the project for the partial reform of the Labor Law tomorrow," Petkoff told reporters.
Reform of the country's Labor Law is the first in a complex series of legislative measures required to revamp Venezuela's crumbling social security system.
The changes, which would include setting up pension funds, are expected to tie up Congress in weeks of debate unless President Rafael Caldera is granted special powers to enact the reforms by decree.
However, Venezuela's largest opposition party, Democratic Action (AD), said on Monday it would oppose such a move (corrects from "would not oppose such a move").

"The constitution shows that one can only use such measures in times of economic or financial emergency, and some think labor law reform is not such a case," party spokesman Aristides Hospedales said.
"We believe the law should first be considered by Congress," he said, adding that the government ought to raise the minimum wage before the reforms are passed into law -- not afterwards.
Under the original terms of the agreement, the government must declare an increase in the minimum wage once the bill is enacted into law.
